speaker: Sheldon
text: Hold. Explain your sneeze. Do you have allergies? Is there too much pepper on your salad? I've heard enough. Sit over there.

speaker: Leonard
text: What? I'm sorry?

speaker: Leonard
text: I don't put pepper on salads.

speaker: Leonard
text: Aw, now I don't want to sit by myself.

speaker: Sheldon
text: That's what Typhoid Mary said, and clearly her friends buckled.

speaker: Leonard
text: Guys, help me. That's just one sneeze. You're on your own.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Shel, then.

speaker: Sheldon
text: See you, buddy. Oh, Leonard, I have something for you. Per our roommate agreement, this is your 24-hour notice that I will be having a non-related female spending two nights in our apartment.

speaker: Leonard
text: When you say non-related female, you still mean human, right?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Of course. Pets are banned under the roommate agreement, with the exception of service animals, such as seeing eye dogs and, one day, cybernetically enhanced helper monkeys.

speaker: Leonard
text: Are you planning on kidnapping a woman?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Sarcasm?

speaker: Leonard
text: Yes, but mixed with genuine concern.

speaker: Sheldon
text: For your information, I'll be playing host to Dr. Elizabeth Plimpton.

speaker: Leonard
text: The cosmological physicist from Princeton?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, and until you acquire a surgical mask, please address your comments to me through a napkin. We've been corresponding for years about our mutual interest in gravitational wave signatures of inflatons in the early universe, and now she's under consideration for a position at our university.

speaker: Leonard
text: Why didn't you tell me you knew Elizabeth Plimpton? I am a huge fan of hers.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I didn't realize I was obligated to share my connection with things you're a fan of, but very well. You enjoy Canadian bacon? I've been to Toronto.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay, fine. Where is she going to sleep? Holy crap!

speaker: Sheldon
text: My room, of course.
